quests.title: The two-minute start
quests.description: Pick the task you've been circling and work on it for exactly two minutes, then stop. Starting is the whole job today; finishing is not required.
quests.encouragement: You started, and starting was the hard part. That counts even if you didn't get far.

quests.title: Send it at 80 percent
quests.description: Take one message, email, or piece of work you keep polishing and send it while it's still 'good enough.' Notice what you were afraid would happen.
quests.encouragement: Done and out in the world beats perfect and hidden. You let something be enough today.

quests.title: One honest no
quests.description: Say no to one small request you'd normally accept out of habit. No long apology, no over-explaining. A simple 'I can't take that on' is a full answer.
quests.encouragement: Turning something down isn't letting anyone down. You protected your yes by using your no.

quests.title: Name one real win
quests.description: Write down one thing you handled today, however ordinary. Then read it back as if a friend had done it, and notice the gap in how you'd judge them.
quests.encouragement: Missed a day? No harm done. The wins were still real, whether or not you wrote them down.

quests.title: A window for the worry
quests.description: When a thought starts looping, jot it on a note and tell yourself you'll think it through at a set time later. Then return to what you were doing.
quests.encouragement: Parking a thought isn't ignoring it. You gave your mind a break, and that's a skill, not avoidance.

quests.title: Cut the list to three
quests.description: Look at today's to-do list and mark only the three things that actually matter. The rest can wait, move, or disappear. Choose on purpose.
quests.encouragement: Three real things beats twelve half-things. Fewer isn't lazy; it's honest about a day's size.

quests.title: Reach out first
quests.description: Message one person you've been meaning to talk to. No agenda, no waiting for the perfect words. 'Been thinking of you, how are you?' is plenty.
quests.encouragement: You closed a small distance today. Whatever they reply, reaching out was the part that was yours to do.

quests.title: Ask for one thing
quests.description: Ask someone for help with one task you'd usually white-knuckle alone. Notice that needing help isn't the same as being a burden.
quests.encouragement: Asking took nerve. Letting someone show up for you is how connection actually works.

quests.title: Five minutes of moving
quests.description: Move your body for five minutes in any way that doesn't feel like punishment. A walk, a stretch, stairs. The point is showing up, not the burn.
quests.encouragement: Five minutes is a real thing, not a failed workout. Something gentle beats an all-or-nothing plan you skip.

quests.title: Reframe one harsh thought
quests.description: Catch one thing you told yourself today that started with 'I always' or 'I never.' Write it down, then ask what a fairer, more exact version would be.
quests.encouragement: Questioning a harsh thought isn't lying to yourself; it's aiming for accurate. One at a time is exactly right.

quests.title: One choice, just for you
quests.description: Make one small decision today based only on what you want, not what someone else would prefer. Where to eat, what to watch, how to spend an hour.
quests.encouragement: You listened to your own preference today. That muscle gets stronger every time you use it, no pressure to be big.

quests.title: Finish one open loop
quests.description: Pick one lingering little task you keep half-doing and take it fully to done. Reply, cancel, book, throw out. Feel the quiet of one loop closed.
quests.encouragement: One loop closed is real relief, not a drop in a bucket. The open ones will still be there when you're ready.
